name: Thorn scrub
notes: Semi-arid thorny woodland/scrub: small spiny legumes and succulents on dry, often thin soils with a sparse grass layer. Drawn on the Caatinga (Brazil), Chaco (Argentina/Paraguay), Tamaulipan thornscrub (Mexico/Texas), Somali-Masai Acacia-Commiphora bushland and Madagascar spiny thicket.

canopy.name: Honey mesquite
canopy.source: Prosopis glandulosa, Tamaulipan thornscrub/Chihuahuan Desert (Mexico, SW USA), thorny deciduous legume 5-12 m — Wikipedia / USDA Plants

canopy.name: Umbrella thorn
canopy.source: Vachellia (Acacia) tortilis, Sahel/East Africa/Arabia, flat-crowned thorn tree of Acacia-Commiphora bushland, 4-14 m — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

canopy.name: Caatinga catingueira
canopy.source: Cenostigma (Poincianella/Caesalpinia) pyramidale, catingueira, dominant deciduous tree of NE Brazil Caatinga, 4-12 m — Flora do Brasil / Wikipedia

canopy.name: Red quebracho
canopy.source: Schinopsis balansae, quebracho colorado, Gran Chaco (Argentina/Paraguay), tall hardwood of Chaco dry forest 10-24 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Baobab
canopy.source: Adansonia digitata, African baobab, dry savanna and bushland of sub-Saharan Africa, massive-trunked deciduous tree 8-25 m — Wikipedia / Kew

shrub.name: Blackbrush acacia
shrub.source: Vachellia rigidula, blackbrush acacia, dominant thicket shrub of Tamaulipan thornscrub (S Texas/NE Mexico), 1-4 m — Wikipedia / USDA

shrub.name: Texas ebony
shrub.source: Ebenopsis ebano, Texas ebony, thorny evergreen shrub/small tree of Tamaulipan thornscrub, 3-8 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Facheiro cactus
shrub.source: Pilosocereus pachycladus, facheiro, blue columnar cactus of the Brazilian Caatinga, 2-6 m — Wikipedia / LLIFLE

shrub.name: Mandacaru
shrub.source: Cereus jamacaru, mandacaru, candelabra columnar cactus of NE Brazil Caatinga, up to 8 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Madagascar ocotillo
shrub.source: Alluaudia procera, Madagascar ocotillo, spiny whip-stemmed tree of the southern Madagascar spiny thicket, 3-12 m — Wikipedia / Kew

shrub.name: Myrrh bush
shrub.source: Commiphora africana, African myrrh, spiny deciduous shrub co-dominant with Acacia in Somali-Masai bushland, 1-5 m — Wikipedia / PROTA

ground.name: Buffelgrass
ground.source: Cenchrus ciliaris, buffelgrass, tufted perennial grass native to Africa/Arabia/India dry bushland, 0.3-1.2 m — Wikipedia / USDA

ground.name: Threeawn grass
ground.source: Aristida purpurea, purple threeawn, wiry bunchgrass of SW USA/N Mexico thornscrub and desert grassland, 0.2-0.7 m — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

ground.name: Prickly pear
ground.source: Opuntia engelmannii, Engelmann prickly pear, pad cactus of SW USA/N Mexico thornscrub, 0.5-2 m — Wikipedia / USDA

ground.name: Elephant's foot
ground.source: Euphorbia tirucalli, pencil tree, leafless succulent shrub of African dry bushland, 1-4 m (larger in cultivation) — Wikipedia / PROTA

ground.name: Kinglet agave
ground.source: Agave lechuguilla, lechuguilla, small spiny rosette indicator species of Chihuahuan Desert and Tamaulipan scrub, 0.3-0.6 m — Wikipedia

epiphyte.name: Ball moss
epiphyte.source: Tillandsia recurvata, ball moss, grey air-plant clumps on mesquite and acacia in Texas/Mexico thornscrub and Chaco — Wikipedia / USDA
